# Development preview — 2026-10-08

An experimental development prerelease of Lapis Obsidian from commit
`79f3b101bc71bb4b8c82f375f2ea921db6e79cc7` (PR #6).

## Included

- Optional embedded HTML5 client, enabled when compiling with
  `LAPIS_OBSIDIAN_WEB_CLIENT=1`.
- Browser terrain rendering, movement, mining and placement, inventory/basic
  crafting, chat, health/respawn and multiplayer support.
- Separate web listener configured by `web-address` and `web-port` in `server.txt`.
- Static Linux/musl builds for AMD64 and 64-bit RISC-V, with and without the web
  client. No Node, Java or downloaded game assets are needed to run the server.

## Choose a download

| File | Architecture | Web client |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lapis-obsidian-alpine-amd64-native.tar.gz` | AMD64 / x86-64 | Disabled |
| `lapis-obsidian-alpine-amd64-web.tar.gz` | AMD64 / x86-64 | Enabled |
| `lapis-obsidian-alpine-riscv64-native.tar.gz` | RISC-V 64-bit | Disabled |
| `lapis-obsidian-alpine-riscv64-web.tar.gz` | RISC-V 64-bit | Enabled |

Extract the matching tarball and run `./lapis-obsidian` from your world directory.
The first startup creates `server.txt`. For a web build, open
`http://localhost:8080/`, or your server's address. Example settings:

```ini
port=25565
web-address=0.0.0.0
web-port=8080
```

Set `web-address=127.0.0.1` for local/reverse-proxy access. Restart after editing.
Native Minecraft clients use port 25565 by default and must be Java 1.21.8
(protocol 772). Both clients share the world. The `native` downloads cannot be
enabled for web access by changing configuration or runtime environment values.

Each binary tarball includes documentation, license/notices and build metadata.
`source.tar.gz` contains the matching source; the individual `.buildinfo.txt`
files describe each variant. Verify downloads with `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS`.

## Validation and scope

All six jobs in the [source build](https://github.com/aksulightning/lapisobsidian/actions/runs/37746522567)
passed: normal/sanitized regressions, live-server and Chromium tests, plus four
architecture/feature builds. RISC-V compilation, startup, configuration and web
transport checks ran under QEMU; hardware performance remains unverified.

This is a development preview. The browser client uses flat-color blocks and
simple entities, with simplified collision and mining. Flight, skins, sound,
particles, sign editing and touch controls are not included. The existing offline
identity model and permissions apply. Direct HTTP/WebSocket traffic is
unencrypted; see the included web-client guide for TLS proxy setup.
